title: Health at home
description: Designed a remote chronic disease management service across UK, Spain, and Brazil, grounded in ethnographic research with patients and nurses. Achieved a 48% reduction in mortality and 63% reduction in hospital readmissions.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: Telefonica Digital / O2, across three markets: O2 UK, Movistar Spain, Vivo Brazil. Cross-functional team of up to 17 people across 5 locations.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Patients with chronic conditions required regular monitoring but hospital visits for routine check-ins were costly and, for many patients, neither feasible nor necessary. Hospital readmission rates were high and preventable. For Telefonica, the business case was proving that health services built on telecoms infrastructure could achieve measurable clinical outcomes — justifying continued investment and commercial rollout.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I led the product and service across the full project: defining the service model, owning the research programme, managing clinical partner relationships, and driving delivery across a cross-functional team of up to 17 people in 5 locations. I was accountable for the product decisions that shaped what the service was and how it operated — not just how it looked.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: The project started with ethnographic home visits across multiple patient groups. The critical insight was that patients didn't talk about the technology — they talked about their nurse. The weekly nurse call was the emotional anchor of the service. This shaped the service model completely: rather than optimising for automation and minimal human contact, I structured the service to protect nurse time for the conversations that mattered most. The clinical workflow was defined with nurses, cardiologists, and heads of department through co-creation sessions. Nurses owned day-to-day monitoring; doctors were brought in only on escalation — a deliberate product decision, not a default.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• 48% decrease in mortality rate among enrolled patients
  • 63% decrease in hospital readmission rate
